content.text: Superpowers is a community plugin, not official: Jesse Vincent and Prime Radiant build it, under the MIT license, in their own GitHub repository. Anthropic's official marketplace lists it, but that catalog also holds plugins from partners and other authors, and a listing doesn't make Anthropic the author. Know what it adds, a skills workflow plus a startup hook, and review it like any third-party code before you install it.

content.text: The half-truth is the listing. Superpowers really is in Anthropic's official catalog. But a catalog says where to fetch a plugin from; it doesn't say who wrote it or promise what it runs.

The repository is plain about it: "Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant." Its plugin manifest names Jesse Vincent as the author, and the license is MIT. Nothing in the repository says Anthropic made or endorses it. The same repo also ships installs for Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and other coding agents, and Prime Radiant offers commercial support for it. It's a popular third-party project that happens to support Claude Code well.

This article describes a third-party plugin. What Superpowers does comes from its own repository, github.com/obra/superpowers, at the time of writing, and it can change. How plugins and marketplaces work comes from the Claude Code docs.

The entry points at the author's repository and a commit. The security docs put it in one line: a marketplace's name "tells you who publishes the catalog, not what each plugin in it does". A review mark doesn't change authorship either. The warning Claude Code shows before an install reads the same for every marketplace: "Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change."
What it adds to Claude Code
The README calls Superpowers "a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable

". Its basic workflow runs brainstorming, a git worktree, a written plan, subagent-driven or inline execution, test-driven development, code review between tasks, and a finish step that offers to merge, open a PR, keep or discard the branch. The README says these are "Mandatory workflows, not suggestions", and its TDD skill "Deletes code written before tests". That explains Monday's surprise.

content.text: Reviewing it before the team turns it on
The tech lead's request was right; the shortcut was skipping it. Compare:

tabs.label: ❌ Wrong
tabs.code:
# "It's official": enabled for everyone in the repo, unread
claude plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official --scope project

tabs.label: ✅ Right
tabs.code:
claude plugin marketplace list   # where each marketplace comes from
git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
claude --plugin-dir ./superpowers plugin details superpowers
cat superpowers/hooks/hooks.json superpowers/hooks/session-start
# Try it yourself first, in this repo only
claude plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official --scope local
